intro: Gordon says there is a separately registered follow-up? Good. We can now investigate the filing system instead of his furniture.
JM-041 is the original mission reference. The recovery and technical examination have their own entries, cross-referenced to it.
I have brought the three records together. Read what each one actually establishes. A missing body is not a death certificate. It is not a forwarding address either.

documents.title: Original mission entry
documents.text:
RECORD CLASS: ORIGINAL MISSION

This entry concerns John's transport assignment. Its initial account did not locate the wreckage and did not contain the subsequent recovery findings.

CROSS-REFERENCES:
JM-041-R — wreckage recovery.
JM-041-T — technical examination.

The original entry must not be read as a complete account of the later investigation.

documents.title: Wreckage recovery record
documents.text:
RECORD CLASS: RECOVERY FOLLOW-UP
RELATED MISSION: JM-041

A subsequent search located the aircraft wreckage.

RECOVERY FINDINGS:
John's body was not recovered.
The transported artifact was not recovered.

These are recovery results. They do not establish that John survived or explain what happened to the artifact beyond its not being recovered.

Technical findings are registered separately as JM-041-T.

documents.title: Technical examination
documents.text:
RECORD CLASS: TECHNICAL FOLLOW-UP
RELATED RECOVERY: JM-041-R
RELATED MISSION: JM-041

Examination established deliberate interference with the aircraft: sabotage.

This record does not identify the person responsible. It does not establish whether John survived.

Any further equipment-accounting inquiry should use the recovery reference, not only the original mission number.

discussion: Three entries, one incident. Different references do not mean three different aircraft. We could not afford that much paperwork.
The records corroborate the later recovery and the sabotage finding. They do not tell us who caused it or where John is.
After your eighth completed agency assignment, ask Alex about the equipment accounting attached to this recovery. Take the cross-reference, not a theory dressed as a conclusion.
